data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes its subject when the test's installation ritual is part of the subject's identity, so the test measures the ritual's own failure handling rather than the subject's response to mutation; the 3-of-26 distribution is a property of the fail-first ritual, not of the guarded modules.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a second independent run with a different first failing mutation produces a different survivor set, the ritual-dependence claim is supported, not refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution is invariant under all first-failure choices, then the ritual is not the generating process and the constraint is elsewhere.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result is reproducible with no installation step at all (pure static analysis), the ritual mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 compile.py survivor is killed when the compile step is run before any registry installation, then its survival depends on installation order.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Shown-to-fail-first installation makes the first failure the reference state. Subsequent mutations are compared not against the clean subject but against a subject already marked as failing. This is a constraint because the comparison baseline is not the subject's behavior but the ritual's memory of the first failure. The 1-of-9 compile.py survival and the 4/4-to-6/7 module scores are then samples from a distribution whose generating process is the ritual's state machine: mutations that land before the first failure are described, those that land after are constrained by the ritual's refusal to re-enter a failed state.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
